<reason>Side A won decisively by dismantling Side B's core economic assumptions and trapping Side B in a fatal contradiction regarding corporate incentives. In R1, Side B claimed companies would buy cheap external credits while simultaneously raising capital for expensive domestic retrofits. Pressured by Side A's Q1, Side B admitted in R2 that no executive would voluntarily pay for expensive internal retrofits when cheap offsets exist—only to contradict itself again in Closing by repeating its R1 claim verbatim. Furthermore, Side A cleanly refuted Side B's assertion that tech and retail value chains are purely domestic, and proved that avoided emissions abroad do not physically neutralize ongoing fossil pollution at home.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's R2 rebuttal [A4.5] dismantling Side B's claim that technology and retail companies lack Global South supply chains by pointing out where smartphones, data-center hardware, and apparel are actually manufactured, coupled with Side A's Q1/R2 trap exposing Side B's contradictory stance on executive incentives.</best_rebuttal>
